title: From Task-Specific AI to Battery Foundation Models
authors: Jingyuan Zhao, Misheng Cai, Yuqi Li, Shengyu Tao, Andrew F. Burke and Stephen Harris
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is influencing battery research and life-cycle management, spanning materials discovery, electrode and cell design, manufacturing optimization, diagnostics, <mark>safety</mark> monitoring, recycling, and certification. These advances are enabled by growing battery datasets and learning methods that extract patterns from complex electrochemical systems. Yet most current models remain task-specific and are trained on fragmented datasets, limiting transferability across chemistries, cell formats, operating conditions, and life-cycle stages.
